subject: Re: Deployment path decision & Dedicated sizing inputs needed
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <skhan@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment path decision & Dedicated sizing inputs needed

Hi Samir — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks to get you a realistic Dedicated proposal.

Summary of what I captured from the call:
- Primary goal: move inference for customer-facing assistant to a production Dedicated deployment for predictable latency and cost.
- Shortlist of models: 7B tuned LLM for session-level RAG + a smaller 2.7B reranker.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~100–130 TPS.
- Burst traffic windows: up to ~350 TPS during launches / marketing spikes.
- Typical token profile: average incoming prompt ~120 tokens, average generated tokens ~700–900 tokens (end-to-end ~820 tokens assumed).
- Latency SLO: p95 response latency target <= 800ms (your note: prefer <500ms if possible for chat flows).
- Data/control: must be VPC-isolated; logs/audit required; SOC2 compliance in procurement.

What we need from you to refine sizing for Dedicated (can be quick bullets):
1) Confirm the steady TPS (range ok) and the expected burst TPS and duration for bursts.
2) Typical percent of responses that use long generation (>=1500 tokens) vs short replies (<300 tokens).
3) Which model family you want prioritized on Dedicated (7B tuned vs 13B opt-in later).
4) Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p95) we should guarantee in the proposal.

Attached is a blank capacity worksheet (capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx) I referenced on the call — if you can fill or send the bullets above I’ll run a couple of SKU mixes and autoscale policies to show cost/latency tradeoffs.

Suggested near-term approach from my side once we get the numbers:
- Initial Dedicated pool sized conservatively to cover steady + 1 mid-sized burst (we typically size for steady * 1.5 then add autoscale headroom).
- Recommend an A100-class node mix for the tuned 7B to hit p95 <800ms; H100 as an upgrade option if you want tighter latency for long responses.
- Configure prefix/KV caching for conversational sessions to reduce token compute where applicable.

Next steps:
- You supply the bullets above or the filled worksheet by EOD Thu 5/21 (if possible).
- I’ll return two SKU mixes (cost-first and latency-first) and a proposed canary plan by Fri 5/22.

Thanks again — appreciate the time.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

From: Samir Khan <skhan@acme.ai>

Subject: Re: Deployment path decision & Dedicated sizing inputs needed

Vivek — thanks for the summary, looks right. Quick answers below to help you size.

- Steady TPS: 105 TPS (measured over last 30 days during normal traffic).
- Burst: short bursts up to 350 TPS, typically 6–12 minutes, seen during feature launches and external campaigns.
- Token mix: ~18% of requests are long-form (>=1500 tokens), 60% are medium (500–1000 tokens), 22% are short (<300 tokens).
- Models: prioritize tuned 7B for now; we will evaluate a 13B variant in Q3 but don’t want to size for it yet.
- Latency: target p95 <= 600ms for standard chat flows; p50 ideally <200ms. If that’s unrealistic for long-form generations we can accept higher for those paths.
- Security: must be deployed in our VPC with HSM-backed keys; SOC2 and penetration test reports required for procurement.

We prefer Dedicated capacity (predictability) but would like a fallback path to Hosted API for sudden multi-hour spikes if you can show cost controls.

I filled the worksheet and attached it (capacity_worksheet_v1_filled.xlsx). Also noted a preference for A100-80GB nodes; our infra team mentioned H100s would be fine if the price delta is reasonable.

Samir

CTO, Acme AI

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment path decision & Dedicated sizing inputs needed

Samir — thanks for the fast turnaround and the filled worksheet. I reviewed the numbers with Karthik and Marissa; below is our recommended near-term plan and open questions.

Recommended initial Dedicated footprint (conservative, can be tuned after canary):
- SKU mix: 6 x A100-80GB (primary pool) + autoscale headroom to add up to 3 additional A100 nodes for sustained higher load.
- Burst strategy: allow burst routing to Hosted API for >380 TPS (policy-based egress) to avoid overprovisioning Dedicated for infrequent long spikes; include throttles and cost alerts.
- Concurrency & batching: target concurrency per A100 gpu = 8 concurrent requests for 7B with our inference optimizations and quantization profile; with your 105 TPS steady and avg token ~820, 6 nodes gives healthy headroom.
- Long-form requests: because ~18% of requests are long-form, we recommend enabling streaming and a separate worker queue to avoid head-of-line blocking. Consider 1–2 H100s as dedicated long-run workers if you want <600ms p95 on long generations (we'll model cost).
- Caching: session-level KV caching expected to reduce token compute by ~10–18% on your workloads; we’ll enable it in the canary.

Open questions / asks:
- Can you confirm the burst duration distribution (you mentioned 6–12 minutes; do you see longer sustained spikes >30mins for events?)
- Do you have a hard budget constraint we need to optimize for (monthly committed spend)?
- Any procurement timelines (SOC2 artifacts needed by legal) we should align to?

Attachments for your review: proposed_sku_mix.pdf (summary of two SKU mixes: cost-first and latency-first) and capacity_worksheet_v1_filled.xlsx (your responses + our assumptions).

Next steps:
1) Quick 30-min follow-up Thurs 5/21 to review the SKUs and canary plan — proposed slots 9:00am or 2:00pm PT.
2) If OK, we’ll provision a 48–72 hour canary on a subset of your traffic (A100 pool of 2 nodes) and collect telemetry.
3) Post-canary we’ll propose final committed Dedicated sizing and an autoscale policy.

If all good I’ll send a formal scoping attachment / SOW draft for procurement.

Thanks — Vivek
